newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Frontpage article supports the decision to establish a socialist market economy in China.
- China will pay greater attention to developing cooperative shareholding enterprises in cities to help develop productive forces.
- A book on the views of Mao Zedong, Deng Xiaoping, and Jiang Zemin is published.
- Total early rice production in central China's Hunan Province is expected to be 17.8 percent more than last year.
- Guangdong police hand over two Vietnamese murder suspects to Vietnamese counterparts.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- China's economy grows at an average rate of 11.6 percent annually since 1992.
- Henan Province purchases 3.5 million tonnes of grain under state quotas this year and spends nearly four billion yuan on another three million tonnes at market prices.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Economist Wang Yu says shareholding system is ideal way to realise public ownership.
- State Information Centre figures show financial deficit to fall 10 billion yuan this year.
- Shenzhen gross domestic product reaches 46.332 billion yuan in first half, up 16.5 percent year-on-year.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China Southern Airlines lists successfully on the New York and Hong Kong stock exchanges, raising $630 million.
CHINA DAILY
- A seminar in Beijing says the Chinese government supports religious freedom and does not discriminate against religious believers.
- Beijing's Association of Relations Across the Taiwan Straits to continue to promote cross-straits exchanges and cooperation.
- 1,700-year-old Dunhuang caves to be protected by laser technology and infra-red photography.
- Yellow River in Shandong Privnce starts to flow again after severe drought leaves it dry for 132 days.
